info.description: One request per endpoint with success and error examples (BE-049). Run in order on a freshly installed database: each step saves the ids the next ones need. Emails, phones and plates use {{$timestamp}} so the collection can run more than once.

item.name: Change job 2's price: job 1 keeps its number and technician

exec: pm.test('{ status, message, data } shape', () => { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j).to.have.keys('status', 'message', 'data'); });

pm.test('same jobs, technician kept', () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.lines[0].line_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('line1'))); pm.expect(d.lines[0].technician_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('techId'))); pm.expect(d.lines[1].line_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('line2'))); });
